'''Johan Frenje''' (born 1967)<ref>{{Cite web |title=VIAF |url=https://viaf.org/en/viaf/596154381057230292383 |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=viaf.org}}</ref> is a Swedish-American physicist who conducts research in the areas of [[High energy density physics|High-Energy-Density Physics (HEDP)]], [[Inertial confinement fusion|Inertial Confinement Fusion (ICF)]], and Inertial Fusion Energy (IFE). Frenje works at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] as a Senior Research Scientist and serves as the Head of the HEDP Division at the [[MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=%s {{!}} MIT Plasma Science & Fusion Center |url=https://www.psfc.mit.edu/about/people/faculty/johan-frenje/ |access-date=2025-09-08 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Frenje earned a Master's Degree in Engineering Physics from [[Uppsala University]] in [[Sweden]] in 1992, followed by a Ph.D. in Applied Nuclear Physics in 1998.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Frenje |first=Johan |date=1998 |title=Instrumentation for fusion neutron measurements and experimentation at JET |url=https://urn.kb.se/resolve?urn=urn:nbn:se:uu:diva-855 |journal=Publications from Uppsala University}}</ref> His work as a graduate student involved the implementation and use of neutron spectrometry in support of the first high-power deuterium-tritium campaign at the [[Joint European Torus]] [[Tokamak]] in 1997.

Frenje was a Postdoctoral Associate at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]] Plasma Science and Fusion Center from 1999 to 2001, before becoming a permanent member of the research staff. In 2013 he was promoted to Principal Research Scientist. In 2017, Frenje gained a promotion to Senior Research Scientist, as well as Assistant Head of the HEDP Division at the Plasma Science and Fusion Center. He later became the Head of the HEDP Division in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Johan Frenje {{!}} MIT Plasma Science & Fusion Center |url=https://www.psfc.mit.edu/about/people/faculty/johan-frenje/ |access-date=2025-09-10 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=New leadership for PSFC High-Energy-Density Physics division {{!}} News {{!}} MIT Plasma Science and Fusion Center |url=http://www-new.psfc.mit.edu/news/2021/new-leadership-for-psfc-high-energy-density-physics-division |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=www-new.psfc.mit.edu}}</ref>

Frenje has been serving on the Executive Committee for the High Temperature Plasma Diagnostics conference since 2014,<ref>{{Cite web |title=25th Topical Conference on High Temperature Plasma Diagnostics HTPD 2024 |url=https://htpd2024.ornl.gov/ |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=Oak Ridge National Laboratory |language=en-US}}</ref> and has been a member of the Scientific Advisory Board for Institute of Laser Engineering at [[University of Osaka|Osaka University]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-09-01 |title=Institute of Laser Engineering |url=https://www.ile.osaka-u.ac.jp/eng/ |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=Institute of Laser Engineering, The University of Osaka |language=en}}</ref> since 2023. From 2015 to 2018, he was the Chair of ICF-HEDP National Ignition Implosion Physics (NISP) Working Group,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Franchot |first=Michael |date=2017-12-11 |title=Workshops at LLE |url=https://www.lle.rochester.edu/workshops-at-lle/ |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=Laboratory for Laser Energetics |language=en-US}}</ref> an effort initiated by the [[National Nuclear Security Administration|National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA)]]. Frenje has also served as Co-Chair and Chair of the Executive Committee of the Omega Laboratory Users Group<ref>{{Cite web |title=Omega Laser Facility Users Group |url=https://www.lle.rochester.edu/about-the-laboratory-for-laser-energetics/omega-laser-facility-users-group/ |access-date=2025-09-09 |website=Laboratory for Laser Energetics |language=en-US}}</ref> between 2016 and 2023; and as a member of the Executive Steering Committee for the National Diagnostic Planning effort,<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ross, Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL), Livermore, CA (United States) |first=J. S. |date=2023 |title=The National Diagnostic Plan (NDP) for HED Science September 2023 |url=https://www.osti.gov/biblio/2008154 |doi=10.2172/2008154 |osti=2008154 |access-date=September 9, 2025 |website=U.S. Department of Energy Office of Scientific and Technical Information|doi-access=free }}</ref> initiated by the [[National Nuclear Security Administration|NNSA]], from 2014 to 2023.

With his students, Frenje builds and operates diagnostics in support of the ICF programs at the [[Laboratory for Laser Energetics]], the [[National Ignition Facility]] (NIF), and the [[Z Pulsed Power Facility]]. At these ICF facilities he has developed his research in high-energy-density [[Plasma (physics)|plasma]] and [[nuclear physics]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Frenje |first=J. A. |date=2011 |title=Measurements of the Differential Cross Sections for the Elastic n−H3 and n−H2 Scattering at 14.1 MeV by Using an Inertial Confinement Fusion Facility |url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.122502 |journal=Physical Review Letters |volume=107 |issue=12 |bibcode=2011PhRvL.107l2502F |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.122502 |hdl=1721.1/68681 |pmid=22026767 |hdl-access=free |article-number=122502}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Anonymous |date=2011-09-15 |title=Pushing toward better nuclear data |url=https://physics.aps.org/articles/v4/s136 |journal=Physics |language=en |volume=4 |issue=12 |pages=s136 |bibcode=2011PhRvL.107l2502F |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.107.122502 |hdl=1721.1/68681 |pmid=22026767 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> In 2022, he and his team contributed to the experimental campaigns at the NIF, achieving ignition and net energy gain.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-12-19 |title=MIT scientists contribute to National Ignition Facility fusion milestone |url=https://news.mit.edu/2022/mit-scientists-contribute-fusion-milestone-1219 |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=MIT News {{!}} Massachusetts Institute of Technology |language=en}}</ref> He has also collaborated with companies in the private sector; such as [[Commonwealth Fusion Systems]], Pacific Fusion,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pacific Fusion – Powering a prosperous planet |url=https://pacificfusion.com// |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=Pacific Fusion |language=en}}</ref> Focused Energy,<ref>{{Cite web |title=FOCUSED ENERGY |url=https://focused-energy.world/ |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=focused-energy.world |language=en}}</ref> and Avalanche Energy.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Compact Fusion Machines {{!}} Avalanche Energy |url=https://www.avalanchefusion.com/ |access-date=2025-09-08 |website=www.avalanchefusion.com |language=en}}</ref>
